words.gloss: right there / at that very moment

parts.gloss: that which lifts up / restores (with poetic lengthening)

literal: That which ruins, and to those who are ruined as a support right there that which lifts up, all is rain.
translation: Rain is that which ruins; and it is also that which, acting as a support, lifts up and restores those who are ruined.
modern: மழை பெய்யாமல் மக்களைக் கெடுப்பதும், வறுமையால் கெட்டுப்போனவர்களுக்குத் துணையாக இருந்து பெய்து அவர்களைக் காப்பதும் எல்லாமே மழைதான்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute power of rain over human life. By withholding itself, rain has the power to destroy livelihoods and cause ruin. Conversely, by falling at the right moment, it acts as a support to revive and lift up those who have been ruined by drought. The poet uses the poetic lengthening (alapedai) in 'கெடுப்பதூஉம்' and 'எடுப்பதூஉம்' to emphasize these two contrasting, yet equally powerful, actions of the rain.
